newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian ANZ job ads rise 2.1 pct in Nov.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian ANZ job ads rise 2.1 pct in Nov.

text.p: The Australia and New Zealand Banking Group Ltd (ANZ) said on Monday that its job advertisement series rose a seasonally adjusted 2.1 percent in November, the first monthly rise since June.
However, job ads were down 11.5 percent on last November and remained negative in trend terms, meaning it was still likely unemployment would reach 9.0 percent in 1997, the ANZ said.

November's 0.8 percent trend decline was up slightly on the 0.7 percent fall in October but the ANZ said this repesented an improvement from the middle of the year when job ads were falling by between 1.6 and 2.0 percent a month in trend terms.
"The slight increase in the number of job advertisements in November is a welcome change from the declines of the previous four months," ANZ chief economist Saul Eslake said.
"However, it would be premature to regard this result as a clear signal of a turning point in labour demand," he said.
Eslake said the trends in job ads were consistent with jobs growth of around 11,000 per month over the next three months, a slight improvement from what earlier data had suggested.

Despite this, it was still below the monthly average of 20,000 needed over the rest of the 1996/97 (July-June) financial year to meet the government's budget forecast of 1.5 percent employment growth.
"It is still likely that the unemployment rate will reach, and perhaps exceed 9.0 percent early in the New Year," Eslake said.
"However, if November's results are repeated over the next few months, that would provide grounds for confidence that unemployment should begin to fall once more."
Seasonally adjusted job ads rose in every state except Western Australia, the ANZ said.
The Australian Bureau of Statistics will release employment data for November on Thursday.
In October, the unemployment rate stood at 8.8 percent.
